properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 by reading reflow2's own founding docs against the build, on Anthony's rule: an already-satisfied doc requirement is dropped, a genuinely new one becomes a proposal. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT EXISTS: `docs/sme-augmentation.md`, a full design dated 2026-07-17. WHAT IS IN THE GRAPH: nothing. No Capability, no Requirement, no detector. Verified — zero occurrences of `sme_consideration` anywhere in the codebase, and `docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ twice (GS-10 "SME gaps", EX-SME "SME augmentation post-pass").

THE IDEA, in the doc's own framing: after faithful extraction, a gated pass in which the LLM adopts expert lenses for the project's domain and operating Environment and surfaces the considerations the user never stated — "You want to build a house on Mars… launch windows, payload mass budget, teleoperated robots vs suited crew, in-situ resource use, radiation and dust mitigation." Each proposal labelled on a grounding spectrum (`verified` / `extrapolated` / `speculative` / `contradicts_known`) with domain, evidence and confidence, landing as a supplementary Fragment at `provenance: inferred` via SUPPLEMENTS, surfaced as `sme_consideration` gaps to accept, edit or dismiss.

⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS ⬜ SUGGESTS. The doc calls it "the capability that most directly serves the vision's premise" — `req:no-se-knowledge` (accepted): the user never needs systems engineering. Every other mechanism reflow2 has REPORTS what the user already said or failed to say. This is the only designed mechanism that would supply expertise the user does not have. Without it, "the user never needs to know systems engineering" is carried entirely by the ambient agent's ad-hoc judgement, unrecorded and ungraded.

⚠️ THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST, and it may be decisive: the agent-native decision (2026-07-18, `dec:` surface-plan) made the ambient coding agent the LLM. An agent reading a brief ALREADY volunteers considerations — that is what agents do. So the question may not be "should reflow2 build an SME pass" but "does reflow2 need to MODEL what the agent already does anyway?" The doc's answer is implicitly yes — the value is the GROUNDING SPECTRUM and the `inferred` provenance, so the user can always tell what they said from what was proposed at them. That is a graph-shaped need, not an LLM-shaped one, and it survives the agent-native decision intact.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Build it as designed — a gated pass emitting `sme_consideration` gaps with the grounding spectrum.
(b) Build only the RECORDING half: a way to mark a node as agent-proposed-not-user-stated with its grounding, and let the skills do the proposing. Much smaller; keeps the honest-provenance value and drops the pass machinery.
(c) Declare it superseded by agent-native capture and retire the doc's requirement rather than leaving it ⬜ forever.
(d) Nothing — it has been ⬜ for over three weeks and no user has asked for it.

NOTE ON RELEVANCE, which is Anthony's actual question: `provenance: inferred` and the SUPPLEMENTS edge both already exist in the schema, so (b) is closer than (a) looks. Whether anyone WANTS this is unanswered — it has never been put to a user, and no friction report has asked for it.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 build SME augmentation, the LLM-as-subject-matter-expert pass? Designed in full 2026-07-17, never built, never in the graph
properties.rationale: The only designed mechanism that would supply expertise the user lacks, rather than reporting what they already said. Fully specified, never built, never in the graph. The agent-native decision weakens the case for the pass but not for the grounded-provenance half, which is the part only the graph can hold.
